purpose: Whole-character idle frame trial; pending visual review
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Reference is the WHOLE approved puppy. Draw a conventional hand-drawn whole-character sprite animation atlas, not a rig and not an illustration of different poses. Exactly SIX columns FOUR rows, 24 equal square cells, landscape 1536x1024 canvas. One full puppy in each cell; order left-right then top-bottom. Genuinely transparent alpha outside the dog. No printed labels, borders, grid, paper, colored matte, shadow, objects or symbols.

Every puppy in ALL 24 cells has EXACTLY the same three-quarter view facing RIGHT, exactly same fixed head orientation and closed smile, same body, same four grounded paws, same size and same scale, same forehead cream blaze, same coat pattern, same green collar and round brass tag. Never mirror, turn left, change camera, tilt the head, resize the head, change facial perspective, move any paw or torso. Full anatomical drawing, no detached parts or human hand gesture. Use the reference's large rounded head, droopy ears, apricot/cream cel shading and chocolate contour, faithfully and consistently. All paws aligned to y=90% within each 256x256 cell, body and face at identical coordinates, clean margins >=8%.

ONLY TWO THINGS ANIMATE: the natural fluffy TAIL and one BLINK, everything else is perfectly stable.
The tail is attached on the LEFT of the body as in the reference. Its fur and curved silhouette are truly redrawn through 24 small in-betweens, never a rigid rotated detached piece. One gentle complete wag loop across the 24 frames:
f1 neutral curved-up tail.
f2-6 incrementally sweep tail outward toward viewer's left until f7 reaches the leftmost position.
f8-12 incrementally return toward neutral.
f13 crosses neutral.
f14-18 incrementally bring the tail slightly behind the rump (partly occluded) until f19 is innermost.
f20-24 return toward original curved-up neutral. f24 is just before f1, no seam.
Tail motion is gentle with easing, no wild swinging and no shape/length flicker.

Blink: f1-9 eyes open exactly as reference. f10 slightly lowering eyelids; f11 half closed; f12 fully closed; f13 half closed; f14 slightly opening; f15-24 open again. Eye position, eye size, irises, nose, mouth, eyebrows and skull stay absolutely registered; only eyelids change. Both eyes blink together.

CRITICAL: every row is a continuation of the same action facing RIGHT. Row3/row4 must NOT show left-facing dogs or a different pose. All 24 dogs have identical naturally seated torso and four-paw anatomy. The first and last images must join seamlessly when played at 12fps. Deliver an animator's conservative consistent idle sprite cycle rather than 24 re-imagined character portraits.
